en.content: Which one of the following statements regarding  Henry's law is not correct ?

options.content: Higher the value of K<sub>H</sub> at a given pressure, higher is the solubility of the gas in the liquids
Different gases have different K<sub>H</sub> (Henry's law constant) values at the same temperature.
The partial pressure of the gas in vapour phase is proportional to the mole fraction of the gas in the solution.
The value of K<sub>H</sub> increases with increase of temperature and K<sub>H</sub> is function of the nature of the gas

en.explanation:
From Henry's law we know,

Pgas = KH xg

Where, Pgas = Pressure of undissolved gas

xg = Mole fraction of gas dissolved into the liquid.

KH = Henry's Carnot.

When pressure is constant then,

xg

So. when KH is high then xg or solubility of gas is lower in the liquid.

So, option (A) is wrong.

en.content: The correct decreasing order for acid strength is :

options.content: NO<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COOH > FCH<sub>2</sub>COOH > CNCH<sub>2</sub>COOH > ClCH<sub>2</sub>COOH
FCH<sub>2</sub>COOH > NCCH<sub>2</sub>COOH > NO<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COOH > ClCH<sub>2</sub>COOH
CNCH<sub>2</sub>COOH > O<sub>2</sub>NCH<sub>2</sub>COOH > FCH<sub>2</sub>COOH > ClCH<sub>2</sub>COOH
NO<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>COOH > NCCH<sub>2</sub>COOH > FCH<sub>2</sub>COOH > ClCH<sub>2</sub>COOH

en.explanation:
After releasing proton (H+) the more stable anion is more acidic nature. The 4 anions are



Here NO2, CN, Cl, F all of them have I effective and all have same distance from the anion ( O).

So depending on which one have more power I effect will be more stable.

Acidic nature I power.

I power order :

NO2 > C N > F > Cl

So, acidic strength order

NO2 CH2 COOH > NC CH2 COOH
> F CH2 COOH > Cl CH2 COOH

en.content: The one that is extensively used as a piezoelectric material is :

options.content: tridymite
amorphous silica
quartz
mica

en.explanation:
Those materials which produce electricity under mechanical stress are called piezoelectric material.

Quartz is an example of piezoelectric material.
